newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH STOCK FALLS ON SALES DISAPPOINTMENT.
newsitem.headline: LVMH STOCK FALLS ON SALES DISAPPOINTMENT.

text.p: Shares in LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton underperformed the weak French stockmarket on Wednesday on disappointment with its cognac business and newly acquired Duty Free Shoppers, analysts said.
LVMH's stock was down 2.76 percent at 1,481 francs at 1010 GMT, while the CAC-40 index was 1.98 percent weaker after a big drop on Wall Street.
Analysts said they were told in a morning conference call with LVMH that half-year cognac sales fell 20 percent in Japan, which represents around a quarter of their global cognac business.
The drop was partly offset by a 10 percent rise in U.S. cognac volumes, but overall cognac and spirits sales fell to 2.34 billion francs from 2.36 billion for the year-earlier period.

Analysts said they were also told that DFS sales fell 10 percent in the first half in dollar terms, due to the yen's weakness. But the dollar's strength meant the revenue was two percent higher when translated into francs. They said DFS's poor performance was due in part to weak travel spending by the Japanese.

Although the cognac and DFS results were disappointing, they were not surprising, analysts said. "I think LVMH is penalised more by the lack of visibility on the Guinness and Grand Metropolitan affair than on the sales results," one analyst said.
After building up an 11.06 percent stake in GrandMet, LVMH appears to have paused in its drive to force the British companies to drop their original merger plan and agree to a drinks deal.
A source close to the French company said further developments in the saga were not expected before the end of the month, after the French summer holidays.
LVMH on Wednesday reported first-half sales surged 62 percent to 21.59 billion francs, boosted by the acquisition of a majority stake in DFS in January.
On a like-for-like basis, however, sales rose 9.4 percent.
Hermes International, whose business approximates LVMH's luxury goods branch, reported a 9.1 percent increase in first-half sales on a like-for-like basis.

Analysts said LVMH's perfume business was hurt as the group fights sales into the parallel market, but they said they were encouraged by the 22 percent rise in sales of Louis Vuitton baggage, the business with the biggest profit margin.
"It wasn't all bad news," one analyst said. The dollar's strength augurs well for future results. "That will kick in later," he said.
